chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Regarding the one who makes a solemn oath (al-mu'li), if he refuses to divorce, he said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would make for him an enclosure of reeds, imprison him in it, and prevent him from food and drink until he divorces.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali)
key_terms.الْمُؤْلِي: The husband who makes a solemn oath of abstention from his wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a husband who refuses to divorce after making a solemn oath of abstention?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the practical enforcement of *ila* (solemn oath of abstention) by narrating Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) method of coercing a recalcitrant husband through confinement in a reed enclosure (*hazira*) and withholding sustenance until he chooses divorce. It highlights the juristic principle of *ikrah* (compulsion) in marital disputes, demonstrating how the Imam applied flexible legal mechanisms to resolve stalemates where the husband refused to exercise his right of divorce. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the Imam’s authority to implement justice through tangible, physical measures when legal declarations alone are insufficient.
